instructor:
Ilyas hoca oldukça bilgili ve müfredaataki ve dışındaki bütün konuları büyük bir heyecanla anlatıyor, gereken yerlerde kendi araştırmalarına da değiniyor. Soru sormaya dersin interaktif geçmesine teşvik etmesiyle derslerin daha keyifli geçmesini başardı. Aynı zamanda derslerle ilgili herhangi bir sıkıntınız olduğunda yarımdımcı olmak konusunda oldukça özverili. Derslerin organizasyonu konusunda derslere gelip takip edildiği sürece hiçbir sıkıntı yoktu. Bu dersin başında kısıtlı bilgim olmasına rağmen sonunda güncel araştırmaları takip edebilecek ve soru sorabilecek düzeye geldim. 

Ilyas Hoca is very knowledgeable and explains all the subjects in the curriculum and outside it with pure enthusiasm, also mentioning his own research where necessary. He managed to make the lessons more enjoyable by encouraging questioning and making the lesson interactive. At the same time, he is very devoted to being a helper when you have any problems with the lessons. There was no problem with the organization of the lessons as long as they came to the lessons and followed them. Although I had limited knowledge at the beginning of this course, I finally came to a level where I could follow current research and ask new scientific questions.

Strongest: He tried hard to get feedback from us at the beginning of classes, and he also tried to encourage us to ask questions in the beginning. He also asked many questions to help us think about the subject. 
Weakest: He did not know what a fourth-year MBG student at Bilkent knew; he had no idea about the previous classes we had taken. It was his first year as an instructor, and he mentioned several times that he did not know bioinformatics. However, this is a genomics course in which we must finish several computational labs. We learned nothing during the class that will help us to do better or understand better the computational labs. Initially, we started with topics that were way below our knowledge, and he asked simple questions that no one intended to answer. Because of this, he started to ask us more questions which we did not want to because we understood the topic well (some of us already knew)—throughout the course, we tried to give him feedback about the slides and overall teaching as a way to help. However, because of this, he started to give us lectures about how we would do poorly as scientists because we did not ask questions in class or approach him (which we did through email and personal visits). There was no answer key while we were looking at our midterm papers. We had to ask each question individually, which he re-read and evaluated in his head and gave a general answer. Because of this, some of us filled in the same answer and got different points. Once we discussed how this is an inefficient way to give feedback, he got offended and treated us as if our only intention was to get more points.

İlyas Hoca is a very idealist instructor who genuinely wants his students to learn more for the sake of learning rather than for grades and passing the course. He always tries to add additional information just so that his students know. He also asks a lot of questions and wants his students to participate a lot in class. 
However, I think his approach could not be too successful in this course due to the lack of motivation of the students. İlyas Hoca would get upset with the students when we didn't show the enthusiasm he expected. I think the students this semester are particularly less enthusiastic as they are almost all graduating. I think it would have been a great learning environment if we could show some more interest or if this class was in earlier semesters.

There are no strong points but many weak points. He doesn't clarify or any clearness about the subject of the class, the lesson, the works , the labs, or the exams all of them were unclear and unprepared. His way of teaching is hard to be called teaching its like he is spitting out what he knows for most of the time. It is just not at the standarts of Bilkent University and made many students unhappy.

He was overall a good instructor with clear interest in the topic. He tried to explain what he knew, and he always tried to learn from the students. One problem was his insistance on questions. He wanted us to ask questions, which I get, but it was sometimes overwhelming. It was a good semester for his first major course, in my opinion.

he loves teaching, you can see with his enthisuasism. Since this is his first teaching experience, he was hesitated a bit and not know our knowledge in biology. The most negative sides of İlyas hoca is that he is not listening while students are trying to explain something to his about lecture/presentation/questions about exam structure. So, I am sure that he will be more comfortable with the students by time but he should really start listening the students. This semester we had a bit conflict, since everybody expected him to create a new syllabus, good lecture content, rich with videos/figures, etc. He literally summerised the four undergrad year, therefore the beginning of the course was boring. I think he should have discussed the content with Ozlen hoca, checked our several courses material to be confident what we have learnt throughout the years, and then build the lecture. By doing this, he would be more confident with the lectures, too. The best part of the İlyas hoca is that he loves his job, very enthisuastic. I hope he will be shining with his love to biology forever!

The instructor has not stated clearly what he expects from us and what we will learn. He demanded we ask questions in the class, but how is that even possible when the lessons are boring and plain? He told us he expects feedback from us, but when we did so, all we got were harsh reactions!
course:
Strongest: with great efforts from TAs, we at least got an idea about how to use computational approaches on genomic analysis (like UCSC genome browser, galaxy, GNOMAD, etc.). Since our instructor is heavily focused on transcription machinery and genetic regulation, we learned excessive information on these subjects.

Weakest: this was a very hard-to-follow course, not because of its topics but because it had two unrelated curriculums. In the official curriculum of the course, the computational lab and in-class course are integrated, meaning you learn what you will do in the lab during the class hour, and then you do it in the lab. However, what we had learned in class had nothing to do with the lab, and it felt like we were following two different curriculums. Most of us expected to learn new approaches and computational approaches to genomics. Still, such approaches were taught by TAs who were no experts and could only give 20-minute presentations or by our instructor on the final few lectures on our demand.
The course material was very detailed for a must-course. I think a sylabus with broader topics with less details would be better for a course like this.
content was poor, less studied on it. I learnt non-coding rnas, but not much other than that.

The course seemed like an overall combination and addition to all that we have learned over the years. It seemed like a very nice way to finish our bachelors degree. 
The course planning was slightly negative, as the last few classes of the semester only contained student presentations of research papers. These were not asked in the exam and attendance was not taken this semester due to the earthquake.Hence, attending these last classes with the presentations seemed very unnecessary and many did not attend. These presentations could be integrated with the lectures more, such as 1 lecture + 1 presentation, so that more people would attend the presentations.
The labs could be better integrated to the course content.
The curriculum of the lectures and the lab hours do not overlap at all.
Probably the technics would be very helpful if it was learned in a different way but it is very hard to say there were any strong points to the class while teached by this instructor.

instructor: Professor İlyas teaches the lessons in a very interactive way. The lesson topics are generally like a repetition of the previous four years, but it is a very informative lesson. Professor İlyas is definitely a teacher who loves teaching and is very successful with the way he teaches the lesson.

İlyas hocam alanına oldukça hakim birisi, derslerine de bu bilgisini yansıtıyor. Fakat genel olarak tekdüze bir anlatım şekli var ve bu belli bir süreden sonra dersten kopmaya neden olabiliyor. Sorulan sorulara da -saçma gözükse dahi- elinden geldiğince cevap vermeye çalışıyor. Derslerinde sık sık sektördeki yeniliklerden bahsetmesi nadiren de olsa konudan sapmaya neden olabiliyor.

Analitik düşünmeyi ve sorgulamayı destekleyen bir insan ancak bazı kişisel değerlerini eğitim pratiklerine yansıttığını düşünüyorum. Özellikle evrimin olmama ihtimaline ve bütün canlıların yaratılışın bir eseri olabileceğine yönelik çok sık vurguda bulundu. Felsefi ve teolojik olarak nitelendirilebilecek bu tartışmanın böyle bir derse dahil edilmesini doğru bulmuyorum.

I think İlyas Hoca is very good and well-equipped in his field. His lessons are generally interactive. Although it may seem reactionary at first that he asks questions and expects answers, when you understand that he does this to encourage learning and to arouse curiosity, the lessons are much more enjoyable and educational. It was very useful for me in completing many missing information and correcting my incorrect information. It is one of the lessons I learned the most among the 4-year MBG lessons. In addition, thanks to the presentations, he showed us what we missed in the articles we read, where we need to pay attention to, that not every article is explanatory and 100% correct, and that we should question.I don't think there is much I can say negatively. It just takes some time to get used to Ilyas Hoca's style at the beginning. If you are going to take the course, my advice would be to attend the class without hesitation.

: I can only list one negative thing. The way his exams work is very different than how the classes work. course: This is definitely a mandatory course; it reinforces all the concepts you've learned in other classes, and you also gain technical knowledge. Many useful websites for lab work are taught.

The contents of the course are very important. There are some repetitive parts, overlapping with MBG210: Genetics, and MBG324: Molecular Genetics, but personally, it was nice to hear the overarching theme and the general idea of contents from İlyas Hoca because only now, I feel like I completely understood them. Maybe the lab session could be lessened of a few sessions, as we repeat the same procedures a lot in different databases. Another suggestion could be to cram everything in 1-2 sessions, and just focus the rest of the lab on RNAseq/NGS data analysis, e.g. on Galaxy, so that we could gain more proficiency with the most important technique.

instructor: Even though İlyas Hoca is responding very quickly, acts very friendly and respectful during conversations, I think he should have explained the concept of thesis, pros, and cons of writing one, thesis format, deadlines, requirements, and evaluation criteria. To explain those, I believe that starting from next year, Zoom meetings should be held once every two weeks or once a month.
course:
As the students who were writing theses, we felt quite left alone... We didn't know the thesis format in a detailed manner, deadlines until very late, etc. As of today (20.05.2025), we still don't know the thesis requirements and evaluation criteria.

To improve this situation, Zoom meetings should be held once every two weeks or monthly. We also need documents explaining the thesis format (in a detailed way), important dates and deadlines, requirements, and evaluation criteria. 

In addition, I think it is unfair that this course is only 5 ECTS. In other universities, thesis work takes up the last year or semester, and students are expected to take no other classes so that they can produce scientifically valuable results or at least improve themselves in the laboratory. So, I think for the following years, this course can be made 6.5 or 7 ECTS, and the students can be promoted to take classes from the upper grades to make up time for this course.

instructor: I think the necessary instructions were not given properly or were changed and not said publicly to all of the students at first, and were revealed much later. I also had trouble receiving a response from İlyas Hoca. This made the process of writing and doing of the project very difficult. Having to finish the thesis suring the finals is also an aggrieving decision. It's not like our thesis will be read before the thesis defense, why could we not submit the report along with the thesis defense?

There was no clear announcement of the exact deadline of the thesis or when the presentations would occur at the beginning of the semester. They were announced 1 month before. Thankfully, Ilyas Hoca was kind enough to extend the deadline for the thesis for one more week. At the beginning of the semester, we were informed that it was planned to be poster presentations, which would be a great opportunity for us since we did not make any posters in other courses, and other students in our department could learn what we have done for our thesis, but apparently, it was decided to go back to presentations. And this decision was not delivered to us until we reached the Ilyas Hoca to learn the dates of the poster presentations. All these uncertainties are improper for a 4th-year course.
course: The thesis project can actually be very useful and beneficial, but having to do a project where certain time and technical constraints are not clearly stated from the beginning is extremely tiring and stressful. On top of that going to the lab and producing a very meaningful project was very difficult.  If you don't have one or two classes left, along with the thesis course, I think not doing the thesis may be more beneficial mentally.

There were no checkpoints for the thesis throughout the semester, but there should be. For example, the literature review can be asked as a report, and a draft can be requested in the middle of the semester. These do not have to be graded, but should be mandatory to pass the course. I think it is in the nature of being a student to delay tasks with deadlines farther in the future. And this course only has 2 tasks that are due at the end of the semester, which causes students to delay. Such intermediate requirements exist in senior project courses of other departments in Bilkent University, other universities in their senior courses, and even in academic essays we wrote in ENG101 and ENG102 courses. I believe the structure of this course does not align with Bilkent University’s standards and would not meet international higher education standards. Thus, the structure of this course should be fixed.

instructor: Frequent deviations from the topic made it harder to concentrate. Since the scheduling was not accurate, he had to finish 3 chapters in one day to make time for presentations. Which, half of the class did for 50 mins and the other half did for 20 mins due to time constraints.

One aspect of Ilyas Hoca that I appreciated was that he taught us about things that were not related to what we were learning in class. While they seemed like they had no relevance at times, it challenged me to actually think about things deeper and even allowed me to make connections between various subjects. It is evident that he is passionate about what he is teaching, and his passion for helping people in some way is very inspirational. One of the best aspects of the course was that it taught us to reevaluate the way that we view research papers.

Something that I did not enjoy about the course was his occasional emphasis on thinking outside the box, which is a great idea, but he often used arguments that were heavy on speculation. One of the concepts that kept getting tossed around was that if something had a low chance of occurring, then it would not occur. Thinking creatively is a good thing, and I appreciate that goal. Still, when an instructor strongly defends ideas without clear proof, I think that crosses a line.

I appreciate encouraging creative thinking, and I agree that questioning ideas is healthy. But when speculative arguments are presented strongly, without solid evidence, it can be misleading. I noticed that some classmates accepted these claims as reasonable, especially since they came from an instructor. For undergraduate students, I think this approach can be confusing and crosses a line.

As someone who loves the field of cancer biology, I was super excited to take this course, but unfortunately, l am quite disappointed with how it turned out. Ilyas Hoca is a respectful and kind professor; however, he couldn't teach us new information about cancer biology at all. He followed the previous instructor's slides, which is perfectly fine, but I believe he didn't study the topics before classes and couldn't deliver the material efficiently. Almost 3/4 of the semester was devoted to p53, and we iterated the same concepts over and over. Bilkent MBG is known for its focus on cancer biology. I believe each of us had quite a bit of knowledge about cancer, coming from previous classes we took. It is absolutely important to explain basic concepts in the beginning, but I don't think that this course was satisfactory for a senior. He wanted us to ask questions, which is great, but we stayed in the same conversation about a single question for almost 30 minutes, occupying a significant portion of the class time that could have been used to learn more about the topic.
Another thing I want to mention is that every student gave an individual paper presentation, but there were no guidelines, and he didn't explain what he expected from us.  As a 4th-year student, I know how to make paper presentations, but I would want to know what kind of grading system he uses. We often couldn't finish these presentations on time because he would take too much time asking questions about the controls or visuals of the figures, which prevented us from understanding the main scientific concepts of the papers. I want to mention one more thing, he gave us a homework, which required talking to a cancer patient in our close circle, asking questions about the mutations and the properties of cancer. I find it extremely insensitive, since some of us lost family members or may be struggling with these in our families, and it might be triggering for us. Overall, I believe it should be improved

İlyas hocanın bu dersi anlatış ve yönetiş şeklini başarılı bulmuyorum. Dersi planlaması çok zayıftı, çok az ders işlendi ve genel sunumlar üzerinden devam even bi program işledi. Ancak sunumların da planlaması zayıf olduğu için dönem başında sunum yapanlar 1 saate varan sunumlar yaparken dönem sonu max 25 dk sunum yapıldı. Derslerde işlenen şeylerin de kanser açısından derinliği yoktu. Daha önceki derslerin kanser ile alakalı kısımlarının birleştirilip yeniden anlatılması gibiydi. Bu yüzden ne yazık ki derslerde yeni bir şey öğrenemedim. Eğer önceki derslerin kanser kısımlarını gerçekten öğrendiyseniz bu dersi almanızı tavsiye etmem çünkü size bir şey katmayacak. Bazı konularda geçmiş derslerde öğrendiğimiz şeylerin konusu açılınca onları da bilmediğini söyledi. Derslerde çok soru soruyor, çok spesifik cevaplar bekliyor ve çok soru sormamızı istiyor. Dersin interaktif olması için bu iyi bir şey gibi gözükse de bu durum her ders 30 dk civarı sürdüğü için ders işlenemiyor ve konular yetişmiyor. Bu sorularla birlikte konun çok dışına çıkıp kanserle alakası olmayan 2. sınıf  bilgileri anlatmaya başlıyor. Bunun dışında bize "yakın çevremizden" bir kanser hastasıyla konuşup genetik testlerini öğrenmemizi isteyen bir ödev verdi. Bunun zaten tek başına tetikleyici bir olay olmasını geçtim, iyileşmiş biri olur mu sorusuna "yakın çevrenizde hiç mi kanser hastası yok?" gibi saçma ve duyarsızca cevaplar verdi. Ayrıca sayısal bölümlerdeki arkadaşlarımla beraber almak motivasyonumu çok düşürdü. Genel olarak bir şey öğrenmedim sadece geçebilmek için uğraştım. Bunun hocayla ilgili değil, direkt dersin kendisiyle alakalı olduğunu düşünüyorum.

Biyoloji okumayan biri olarak bir dönem içine sığdırılmaya çalışılan konular çok fazla. Bu yüzden 3 saatte bir ünite öğrenmeye çalışmak çok zor. Sınavlar da fazla detay ve sanki seçmeli bir ders değil de bölüm dersiymiş gibi yorumlanmadı beklenen tarzdaydı.

I liked the content of the course. However, there are some problems with the structure of the course in my opinion. It is very centralized, as our teacher did not have much idea of the assignments. Also, there was a huge problem with our class, the projector had problems. Our teacher talked to the superintendent, etc. We had this problem for the first 2-3 weeks, and it occurred again at the end of the semester, and because of that, we couldn't do our class. It is a surprising problem to face at Bilkent University; we couldn't do class because the projector did not work.

Vizeler finalden 1 hafta önce açıklandı ancak. Ödevler hakkında son haftaya kadar bir bilgi verilmedi.Sınavların tarzı garip ve bazıları çok da bilgi ölçer nitelikte değildi bence daha iyi bir fomatta hazırlanabilir.Ve bazı soruların açık olduğunu düşünmüyorum, fazla yazınca da nedense bir puan kırılıyor.Genel olarak zor bir ders değil ama iyileştirilebilir.Ders hakkında sadece koordiantörün bilgi sahibi olmasını doğru bulmadım, kendi hocamız çoğu şey için koordinatöre yönlendiriyordu.
Bölüm başkanımız öğrencilerinden nefret ettiği için COMD bölümündeki herkesin hayatını cehenneme çevirmek için seçmeli olarak zorunlu tuttuğu bir ders.
